subject: MAP: cost & unit-econ verification (tokens/$, caching, batching)
messages:
From: Alex Thornton <alex@lumenix.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & close timeline — need unit-econ check

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we finalize the MAP and lock a close date, procurement asked that we validate the unit economics for the pilot and first 3 months of production. Specifically they want: tokens/$ assumptions, how caching and prefix reuse will reduce billed tokens, and realistic batching gains for latency-sensitive routes.

We have a predictable traffic spike pattern (hourly QPS ~ 45–90, baseline 15) and expect average user prompt length ~ 60 tokens with an average model response of ~ 220 tokens. We need a quick sanity check to confirm this won't blow our monthly spend.

Could you and your engineering lead confirm the following and add to the MAP:
- Tokens-per-interaction (prompt + response) used for cost calc
- Expected cache hit rates (prefix or session-level) we should budget
- Batching behavior for 95th percentile latency under our traffic profile
- Any recommendations to reduce tokens/$ (quantization, smaller variants, prefetch, etc)

Attached is our rough traffic export if that helps (attached: traffic-sample.csv). Happy to jump on a call.

Alex
CTO, Lumenix

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Alex Thornton <alex@lumenix.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close timeline — need unit-econ check
Attachments: lumenix-map-draft.pdf

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've sketched a MAP attachment (lumenix-map-draft.pdf) that folds in a cost-validation checkpoint before the pilot sign-off. Quick summary here so procurement can see high-level assumptions up-front:

1) Baseline tokens per interaction: 280 tokens (60 prompt + 220 response). We'll present sensitivity +/- 20% to cover richer prompts.
2) Caching: assume 35% prefix reuse on chat flows where the user repeats structured prompts; conservative estimate 20–50% as a range.
3) Batching: with our Dedicated runtime and your traffic profile we see batching windows that yield ~1.7x tokens/sec efficiency at median load and up to 2.4x at peak if requests are bursty and can tolerate ~15–25ms queueing on non-latency-critical routes. For latency-sensitive routes we recommend smaller batch windows (~2–5ms) with limited gains (~1.1x).
4) Cost levers: lower-cost model variants for low-risk assist tasks, 8-bit quantization for internal-only models, and prefix caching on the most common templates.

Marissa (SE) — can you validate the batching/cache numbers and add any GPU/quantization notes?
Karthik — can you call out any limits on concurrency that would change these assumptions and a recommended guardrail for MAP?

I'll update the MAP with an explicit tokens/$ page once we have your numbers. Proposed next step: 30-min cost-runthrough tomorrow 10:00 PT.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, Alex Thornton <alex@lumenix.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP & close timeline — need unit-econ check
Attachments: none

Alex / Jordan —

I've run a quick back-of-envelope based on the sample traffic Alex shared and our internal telemetry for similar customers. Key assumptions and recommended MAP gates below (I put numbers you can drop directly into the MAP).

Assumptions
- Mean prompt tokens: 60 (range 40–120)
- Mean response tokens: 220 (range 100–400)
- Interactions/day: assume 20k active interactions for pilot month (scale as you provided)

Tokens per interaction (base case): 280 tokens
Tokens per interaction (with 35% cache hit on response prefix): 182 tokens (280 * (1 - 0.35))

Billing scenarios (hosted token pricing examples) — use these to populate tokens/$ sensitivity table in the MAP:
- P1: $0.000012 / token (full model, hosted) => 280 tokens ≈ $0.00336 / interaction
- P2: $0.000009 / token (quantized variant) => 280 tokens ≈ $0.00252 / interaction
- P3: Effective after caching (35% hit) at P1 price => 182 tokens ≈ $0.00218 / interaction

Batching notes (derived from our Dedicated runtime tests):
- For conversational API (short-lived sessions) with 50–100 QPS: set batch window 12–20ms to capture inter-arrival bursts; expect 1.5–1.9x throughput improvement (decreases per-token compute cost) without increasing median latency beyond ~15ms.
- For strict 95th percentile latency < 200ms routes, use 3–5ms windows and set max batch size = 8; expect ~1.05–1.2x throughput benefit.

Operational MAP gates to include
- Gate 1 (Pre-pilot): cost sanity check — projected monthly token spend delta across 3 pricing scenarios; green = within budget, amber = requires model variant plan, red = renegotiate scope.
- Gate 2 (Pilot week 2): measured cache hit rate vs expected (if < 20% -> action: increase template usage / session affinity).
- Gate 3 (Pre-prod): 95th pctl latency with production traffic simulator; if batch window gains require >25ms additional queueing on critical paths -> require fallbacks to smaller model or Dedicated reservation increase.

I'll add a small table to the MAP with the three billing scenarios and a checklist for who signs off at each gate.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, Alex Thornton <alex@lumenix.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & close timeline — need unit-econ check
Attachments: batch-profile.csv

Quick additions from infra side —

1) Concurrency & GPUs: If you want the higher batching gains (>=1.7x), we'll recommend Dedicated pool with A10x8 style nodes (4–8 GPUs depending on headroom) and a pinned model variant. Shared-hosted routes see more variance; plan +20% capacity headroom at peak.
2) Quantization: 8-bit quantization gives ~30–35% reduction in compute cost; quality drop is model-dependent — recommend a two-track eval (quality vs cost) inside the MAP.
3) Cache semantics: prefix caching works best for structured templates and identical continuations. Session-KV caching increases hit-rate but needs sticky routing (we can define this in the MAP as an ops requirement).
4) Batch-profile.csv (attached) contains simulated batching outcomes for your sample traffic (columns: qps, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, effective_throughput_gain). Use the p95 latency column to decide gate thresholds.

If you share estimated monthly RU (requests) and an AOV for interactions we can build a quick tokens/$ projection to paste in the MAP. Kicking off the short call tomorrow is fine — I can bring an infra cost slide.

-Karthik
Senior Platform Engineer — Redwood Inference
